chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abdullah al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Zurara, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the grave, how many can enter it? He said: That is up to the guardian; if he wills, he will allow an odd number, and if he wills, he will allow an even number.
ai.seo_question: How many people can enter a grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical capacity of the grave, noting that the number of souls entering is not fixed but determined by the will of the *Wali* (often interpreted as the Imam or God). This flexibility, allowing for either odd (*watr*) or even (*shuf*) numbers, reflects the divine power to expand or contract the spiritual space of the grave according to the status of the deceased. It underscores the Shia belief in the active, dynamic nature of the grave (*Barzakh*) as a realm governed by divine decree and intercessory authority.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Abdullah Al Hajjal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, 
from Zurara who asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

about the grave, how many can enter into it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is up to the guardian (of the deceased). If he so desires to he can (allow) an odd number, and if he so desires to he can (allow) an even number (of people)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ‘Abd Allah al-Hajjal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Zurarah who has said the following: “I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
How many should enter a grave?’ He replied, ‘It is up to the guardian of the deceased. He may ask an odd or even number of people.’”
